name: Lake Ohrid Region
blurb: A clear, ancient lake with over 200 endemic species, from trout to snails.
notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light drives the algae of the clear lake, the reed beds and the crops and vines of the shore.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae, reeds, fish and land animals, returning nutrients to the water and soil.
Forms reed beds along wetland shores. Most Ohrid shore wetlands have been drained, and the reed belt is under pressure from building.
Tiny crustaceans of open water. Ohrid has about five endemic zooplankton species. General ecology: they graze algae.
A common small rodent of the shore scrub and fields that eats crop seed such as maize and is prey for many predators.
Eats fish and molluscs at night. Dams on the Drin block its return, so Ohrid eels are stocked.
A big fish-eater among the waterbirds that winter in the Ohrid reed beds. Wetland drainage caused its decline.
Large water frog of lakes and rivers. Mostly eats invertebrates but also takes small fish and other amphibians.
Water snake of lake shores, recorded very often near Ohrid. It often eats fish and sometimes frogs and toads.
Omnivore. GloBI records link it to rodents, frogs, snakes and grapes.
Generalist that eats rodents, frogs, snakes and fruit, per GloBI records.
Top predator of the surrounding mountains, with GloBI records of it eating rodents, foxes, martens and snakes.
Omnivore of the mountains. GloBI records show it eating rodents, foxes, grapes and maize.

story: Lake Ohrid straddles the mountainous border between North Macedonia and Albania. It is one of Europe's deepest and oldest lakes, containing clear water and more than 200 endemic species.
matters: It has a unique aquatic ecosystem of worldwide importance. The lake shelters numerous endemic species, including the Ohrid trout and the Dalmatian pelican.
